title: Archive and Gravity
premise: Wendell Quintana has spent nine years alone on Kepler-442c, tending a terraforming garden for colonists who will not arrive for another century and maintaining a beacon whose original commission records have been quietly erased. When a distress signal arrives in Vessic — a language extinct since the Collapse — she discovers the beacon was built to receive it, and that someone in the fleet deliberately buried that fact. Pursuing the signal to the relay at the edge of dead space, Wendell falls in with the crew of the salvage ship Perihelion, a ragged found family who teach her that loyalty and truth are not the same thing. As the fleet's fragile truce expires, Wendell must choose between exposing the archive of erased histories hidden in her own beacon — which could reignite the war — or letting the dead language, and the last survivors speaking it, vanish forever. She chooses a third path: broadcasting the truth to everyone at once, forcing the fleet to reckon with it in the open, and finding that the family she made along the way chooses to stand with her.
about_author: Mirabel Thackeray is a former botanical archivist who spent a decade cataloguing seed banks before turning to fiction full-time. She writes from a converted greenhouse on the Atlantic coast, where she grows heirloom plants nobody has requested in fifty years.

chapters.title: The Garden of Unborn Weather
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. Establishes her solitary life: pruning engineered pines, logging soil data, speaking aloud to no one. The beacon pulses its routine heartbeat until one night it answers something back — a distress call in Vessic, a language she only knows from forbidden archive fragments. Emotional beat: loneliness cracked open by impossible contact.

chapters.title: A Commission Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Wendell digs into the beacon's maintenance logs and finds the commissioning records scrubbed — replaced by her own name, retroactively. A fleet survey drone arrives to 'recalibrate' the beacon; she hides the signal intercept inside the garden's irrigation core. POV alternates with brief interludes from the signal itself. Beat: paranoia taking root alongside wonder.

chapters.title: Dead Space, Live Signal
chapters.summary: Wendell abandons the garden to the automated systems and takes her aging skiff toward the relay at the edge of dead space, following the signal's bearing. Her navigation fails in the gravitational shoals; she is scooped up mid-drift by the salvage ship Perihelion. Beat: terror giving way to the disorienting warmth of other people.

chapters.title: The Crew of Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Perihelion's POV ensemble: Captain Oyelaran, engineer twins Sefa and Bram, and archivist-pilot Juno, who recognizes Vessic on sight and goes pale. They're running black-market memory cores under truce cover. Wendell conceals why she's really out here. Beat: found family forming around shared secrets neither side fully trusts.

chapters.title: What the Truce Buried
chapters.summary: Juno's POV. She reveals the Vessic were not extinct but displaced — their colony ships scattered into dead space, their language outlawed by the armistice that ended the war. The distress call comes from one such ship, still drifting, still alive. The fleet's truce expires in nineteen days. Beat: grief for a history Wendell was raised inside of without knowing.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Wendell's POV. The crew debates: answer the call and risk war-crimes charges, or sell the signal's location to the fleet for amnesty. Wendell realizes her beacon wasn't just a receiver — it was an archive, holding every record the armistice erased, including proof of who ordered the Vessic scattering. Beat: loyalty to new friends colliding with the truth she carries.

chapters.title: The Relay at the Edge
chapters.summary: En route to the drifting ship, the Perihelion is boarded by a fleet inspection cutter. Wendell uses her official terraformer credentials — the identity she resents most — to talk them through, lying fluently for the first time in her life. Bram is injured covering for her. Beat: identity as both cage and weapon; guilt braided into belonging.

chapters.title: Ship of the Living Language
chapters.summary: They reach the Vessic vessel Meridian of Salt: two hundred survivors, three generations born in drift, children who speak the outlawed tongue as their only language. Their elder, Iyo, tests Wendell by asking her to read the archive fragment she carries aloud. Beat: awe and shame — Wendell meets the people her silence helped erase.

chapters.title: Expiry
chapters.summary: Climax. The truce expires as the fleet arrives to seize the Meridian. Wendell broadcasts the full archive — every erased record, every signature — through her own beacon network, making concealment impossible and forcing open negotiation rather than quiet massacre. Oyelaran positions the Perihelion between the guns and the drifters. Beat: truth deployed not as betrayal but as the only loyal act left.

chapters.title: Gravity, and What It Keeps
chapters.summary: Resolution, Wendell's POV. Months later: ceasefire renegotiated, the Meridian granted a corridor home, the archive public. Wendell returns to Kepler-442c with Juno and Sefa aboard, planting the first Vessic seed-stock in the garden meant for people not yet born — now including people who survived being forgotten. Beat: identity remade; gravity as love, the force that keeps you in orbit.
